subject: Lame duck president
query: what is a lame duck president
title: What is a lame duck president? The term, explained
answer: A lame duck president is one whose time in office has a known end date, so his influence is expected to fade. The term is used for a president who lost re-election or did not run, in the weeks before a successor takes over, and more broadly for a president in a second term, who cannot run again under the 22nd Amendment.
body:
The 22nd Amendment says "no person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice," and someone who served more than two years of another president's term can be elected only once. Congress proposed it on March 24, 1947, and it was ratified on Feb. 27, 1951, after Franklin D. Roosevelt won four presidential elections. Britannica notes that presidents who win a second term are often called lame ducks and that the race to succeed them often starts even before their second inauguration.

The phrase "lame duck" was first used in 18th-century Britain for bankrupt businessmen, and by the 1830s it was applied to officeholders whose time in office had a known end. The same idea gives the "lame duck session" of Congress, which meets after a November election but before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3.

Donald Trump began his second, nonconsecutive term on Jan. 20, 2025, so under the 22nd Amendment he cannot be elected president again; his term ends at noon on Jan. 20, 2029. Separately, the outgoing Congress began its lame duck session on Nov. 9, 2026, after midterms in which, according to the AP, Democrats won control of both chambers.
in_the_news: "Lame duck" is in the news as Congress returns for its post-election lame duck session on Nov. 9, 2026, after midterms in which Democrats won both chambers.

faq.q: Why is it called a lame duck?
faq.a: The phrase began in 18th-century Britain for bankrupt businessmen and was later applied to officials whose time in office was ending.

faq.q: Is Trump a lame duck president?
faq.a: He is serving his second term, and the 22nd Amendment bars anyone from being elected president more than twice, which is why commentators use the term for him.

faq.q: When does a president become a lame duck?
faq.a: Traditionally after losing or not seeking re-election, and more broadly once a president is in a final term that cannot be extended.

faq.q: What is a lame duck session?
faq.a: A meeting of Congress held after the November election but before the new Congress takes office on Jan. 3.
